screenLevelGaps: ANSWER 1 — LMS certificates vs Competency Certifications are two unrelated stores of the same concept. Verified by grep: `lms_certificates` appears ONLY in app/Http/Controllers/Api/LmsLearningController.php (12 sites); `s_competency_certifications` appears only in Competency controllers, CompetencyCertification model, skillLibraryController and CommandCenterService. Neither reads the other. s_competency_certifications has no course_id / certificate_id / source column (see migration 2026_07_29_110100 which adds certification_type, verification_status, verified_by/_at, notes, requirement_id — none referencing LMS), and CertificationItem exposes only a free-text `credential_id`. So an LMS-issued credential is invisible to Competency's compliance KPIs, its requirement matching, its verify/reject workflow and its evidence repository; and a Competency-registered credential is invisible on this screen. Two registers, two expiry engines, two 'expiring soon' windows, two verification models — exactly the 'duplicated build' the customer's own Integration Points forbid.

ANSWER 1b — the single link that does exist is decorative. lms_certificates.skill_id is populated at issue via resolveCourseSkillId (LmsLearningController.php:965-984) and joined to s_users_skills for one sentence in the drawer: 'Counts towards {skill} in the competency framework' (certifications-records.tsx:616-623). It is prose. Issuing or re-issuing a certificate writes nothing to s_skill_matrix, creates no s_competency_certifications row, and satisfies no s_competency_certification_requirements row. Combined with the known ground truth that no LMS controller writes s_skill_matrix, LMS 'build skill' produces no measurable change in Competency's 'measure skill'.

ANSWER 2 — Governance administers: tbluser (users), tbluserprofilemaster (roles), tblmenumaster + tblgroupwise_rights (permission matrix), lms_trainers, lms_vendors, lms_integrations, and reads hpbrain_audit_logs. The Settings tab administers nothing.

ANSWER 2a — THE PERMISSION MATRIX EDITS THE WRONG TABLE. LmsGovernanceController::permissions() reads tblmenumaster (line 943) + tblgroupwise_rights (line 954) and savePermissions() writes tblgroupwise_rights (lines 1041-1050). The Next.js product's sidebar and route access come from tblmenumaster_g2g + tblgroupwise_rights_g2g via GET /user/ajax_sidebar_menu_g2g (routes/user.php:43-44 -> tblmenumasterG2gController::displaySidebarMenu), and content-map-m4.ts keys every LMS route on the tblmenumaster_g2g access_link. Different tables, different models (tblmenumasterModel vs tblmenumaster_g2gModel; tblgroupwise_rightsModel vs tblgroupwise_rights_g2gModel). Toggling any checkbox in the Permission Matrix, clicking Save Changes, and seeing 'Saved N permissions' changes NOTHING about what a role can reach in the application being sold. The correct endpoints already exist and are simply not called: /user/ajax_groupwiserights_g2g and /user/save_groupwiserights_g2g (routes/user.php:45-48). The Roles table's 'Menus visible' count and the 'Permissions — rights assigned' KPI are computed from the same legacy table and are equally meaningless.

ANSWER 2b — role enforcement IS real at the API, but is inconsistent and name-based. Every write in LmsGovernanceController and LmsPartnerController is guarded by guardAdmin, and identity/tenant/actor all come from the token (ResolvesLmsIdentity), so the previously-documented `user_profile_name` spoof is genuinely closed. Three problems remain: (i) the allowed sets differ per controller — Governance and Partners allow ['admin','hr','super','principal'] while Sessions and certificate re-issue allow only ['admin','hr'], so a 'principal' can create users, roles, permissions, trainers, vendors and integrations but cannot schedule a training session; (ii) matching is str_contains on the lowercased profile name (ResolvesLmsIdentity.php:100-104), so a role named 'Administrative Assistant' matches 'admin' and any name containing the letters h-r (e.g. 'Chronicler') matches 'hr' — and roles are created from this very screen with a free-text name field; (iii) the client gate is a different function entirely — canAdminister = user.role === 'admin' || 'hr' where role is derived by mapProfileNameToRole (lib/laravel-session.ts:80-97), so a real 'principal' sees a read-only screen the API would let them write, and AuthContext exposes switchRole() which lets any client flip user.role locally and reveal admin controls (harmless, since the API refuses, but it means UI role state is not a security boundary).

ANSWER 2c — reads are under-guarded. kpis (line 150), roles (line 712) and systemHealth (line 1176) have guardApiToken but NO guardAdmin; trainers (LmsPartnerController:380 region), vendors and integrations are likewise token-only. Any authenticated tenant user can read the org's user/role counts, the full role list, vendor contract values, and System Health. The 'Active Tokens' health check is not tenant-scoped at all — it counts personal_access_tokens platform-wide.

GOVERNANCE AUDIT IS ONE CONTROLLER DEEP. Only LmsGovernanceController writes hpbrain_audit_logs (insert at line 102). Nothing in LmsSessionController, LmsPartnerController or LmsLearningController audits anything, and no Competency/Talent/Task/HRIT controller does either. So the 'Audit Logs' tab records user/role/permission changes made through this screen and literally nothing else — not trainer or vendor or integration CRUD from the adjacent tabs, not session creation or cancellation, not certificate issue or re-issue, not enrolment or assignment. The spec's 'audit logs (who completed/edited/assigned what)' and 'data export for external audits (ISO, regulatory)' are not met. Compounding it: actor_name stores the profile name not the person, status is hardcoded 'success' so failed privileged attempts are never logged, and the `changes` JSON is written but never selected or displayed.

SESSIONS PRODUCE NO EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. lms_session_registrations is read exclusively by LmsSessionController — no other file in app/ touches it. The status enum includes 'attended' and 'no-show' but no endpoint or control ever sets them, so instructor-led training cannot be marked as attended. Consequently ILT yields: no course enrolment (subject_id is never sent by the form despite being validated and written by the controller), no completion, no certificate, no transcript line, no HRIT attendance record, and no competency signal. In ownership-model terms, the entire 'classroom/virtual delivery' half of LMS = BUILD skill is a scheduling calendar that terminates in itself.

THE TRAINER REGISTRY AND THE SESSIONS IT EXISTS FOR ARE UNLINKED. lms_virtual_classroom.trainer_id was added specifically to fix this (migration 2026_07_29_110001) and LmsPartnerController reads it, but grep across app/Http/Controllers shows NO controller ever writes it — LmsSessionController::rules() (lines 645-664) and payload() (lines 668-685) omit it entirely, and the session form has no trainer picker. The only rows with trainer_id are those the migration's one-time email backfill claimed. Every session created from now on lands in the 'unlinked_session_count' fuzzy-match bucket.

CROSS-SCOPE CONTRADICTION ON THE RECORDS SCREEN. For an admin/HR user the Certificates and Renewals tabs are org-wide (scope=all, tenant-scoped server-side) while the Learning Transcript and Completion History tabs are hard-scoped to the caller (/api/lms/learning/courses uses the token user; /api/enrolled_courses is caller-supplied). The page subtitle says 'Certificates and completion records across your organisation' and the tab badges sit side by side, so HR sees 4,000 org certificates next to their own 3 completed courses. 'Download Transcript' therefore exports the HR user's own transcript — the spec's 'employee learning transcript generation' cannot be performed for anyone else from this screen.

SECURITY — IDOR on the Learning Transcript data source. GET /api/enrolled_courses resolves the tenant from the token but takes the subject from the request: `$userId = $request->user_id ?? $request->header('user_id')` (app/Http/Controllers/lms_course_enroll/LmsCourseEnrollController.php:39). withLaravelParams always sends user_id, so any authenticated user can substitute another employee's id and read their full enrolment history. Every other endpoint on these three screens correctly uses contextUserId() from the token; this one was missed.

BULK USER IMPORT CREATES UNUSABLE, UNPLACED ACCOUNTS. IMPORTABLE_USER_COLUMNS (LmsGovernanceController.php:659) excludes department_id, job role and reporting manager, so imported people have no org placement — the Integration Points requirement that a new hire's role/job-profile triggers competency framework mapping and an onboarding learning path cannot fire. And the panel's promise that 'each user gets a random password to reset on first sign-in' is false: the controller bcrypts random bytes (line 656), sends no mail (the file imports no Mail/Notification facade) and sets no must-reset flag, so every imported account is locked out with a password nobody knows.

INTEGRATIONS ARE A BOOKKEEPING TABLE, NOT INTEGRATIONS. storeIntegration/updateIntegration record a provider name and a status string and explicitly accept no credential (LmsPartnerController.php:617-620 and the migration rationale). Marking Google/Okta 'connected' does not change login; marking Zoom/Teams 'connected' does not create meeting links (the session form still requires a hand-typed URL); marking SCORM Cloud 'connected' does not enable SCORM ingest. The spec's 'Integration management (HRIS, SSO, video conferencing tools)' — and HRIS sync for bulk enrolment — has no implementation behind this UI.

SETTINGS TAB CONFIGURES NOTHING. It renders eight read-only counters and a vendor-contract list. None of the LMS spec's System Configuration items exist anywhere: course expiry & re-certification cycles (validity lives on sub_std_map, editable only in the course builder), mandatory/compliance training rules engine, catalog visibility rules by department/location/grade, branding/white-labelling, multi-language content. Even the certificate 'expiring soon' window that the Records screen displays is config('lms.certificate_warning_days') — a global env value, not per-tenant and not editable by an administrator.

DEAD OR UNREACHABLE CAPABILITY ALREADY BUILT ON THE SERVER: PUT /governance/roles/{id} (no Edit control exists — roles can be created and deleted but never renamed); user list department_id filter and sort_by/sort_dir (supported, no controls); trainers ?search= (service parameter always undefined, no search box); TrainerPayload.user_id_link, .bio, .qualifications (no controls); VendorPayload.website/address/notes and currency (no controls; currency hardcoded INR); audit-logs search/entity_type/from/to filters and the returned filters.entity_types list (stored in state, never rendered); lms_certificates.name/description/tags per-certificate editing (designed as editable, no UI); session subject_id (validated and written, never sent).

DESTRUCTIVE ACTIONS WITHOUT CONFIRMATION: Remove trainer (governance-panels.tsx:470-479), Remove vendor (666-675), Remove integration (830-839) and Remove attendee (sessions-calendar.tsx:699-713) all fire on a single click. Users, roles and sessions do have confirmations, so the inconsistency is a UI oversight rather than a pattern.
